answer: Quill-Tagged Entry Lottery. Each epoch the protocol draws a verifiable random beacon; an identity registers only by submitting a quill mark that satisfies the beacon-derived target, and each accepted mark occupies one slot in a bounded grove of active agents. Because the beacon is revealed only after the epoch opens, an attacker cannot precompute marks or batch-generate clones offline. Winning a slot costs one full epoch of sustained compute per identity, and slots expire at the horizon, forcing repeat expenditure.
